issues.body: `preceded_by_name` delegates ordinary ASCII continuation bytes to `transpile::is_ident_char`, which omits legal PN_LOCAL punctuation such as `-` and internal `.`. Thus valid terms such as `ex:a-selct` or `ex:a.selct` expose `selct` as a candidate after the punctuation and can incorrectly suggest `SELECT`. The new parser-backed test covers Unicode and backslash escapes, but not these standard PN_LOCAL continuations, so the round-one correctness issue is only partially fixed.
issues.fix_hint: Make both candidate boundaries follow the complete vendored PN_LOCAL lexical rules, including `-`, internal `.`, percent escapes, PN_LOCAL_ESC, and Unicode, rather than treating only non-ASCII and backslash as additions to `is_ident_char`. Add real-parser-backed regressions for valid prefixed names such as `ex:a-selct` and `ex:a.selct`, asserting parsing succeeds and `keyword_hints` is empty; retain a bare-typo positive control.
issues.title: Valid prefixed names containing hyphens or dots can still produce keyword hints

verdict.summary: Round 2 fixes the reported Unicode and PN_LOCAL_ESC examples with real-parser-backed tests, but the same major false-positive class remains for ordinary legal PN_LOCAL punctuation. `is_name_byte` claims the only missing name-byte classes are non-ASCII and backslash, yet `PN_CHARS`/`PN_LOCAL` also allow `-` and internal `.`, neither of which `transpile::is_ident_char` accepts. Consequently an ASCII keyword-like suffix after either punctuation is still scanned as a standalone typo inside a valid prefixed name. The public guarantee that every valid query produces no hints is therefore still unmet.
